correctness.rationale: The explicit three-dimensional orthogonal frame gives weighted-cosine Frobenius square 197/40 against conjectured bound 63/13, an exact positive gap 41/520. A symbolic factorization proves a continuum of violations for spectra diag(t,1,t^-1) with t>=3/2; an embedded order-four example gives gap 13/40. A separate determinant-and-trace argument proves the conjectured inequality for every real orthogonal pair in dimensions one and two. The included exact-symbolic artifact checks the algebraic identities.

originality.rationale: The September 2026 source manuscript states the upper bound as a numerically suggested conjecture and currently lists only arXiv v1. No located erratum, comment, or literature source gives this counterexample, robust family, order-four violation, or minimal-dimension theorem. Classical frame-potential results concern minimization rather than this spectrum-dependent upper bound, and the claim is explicitly limited to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result refutes an explicit structural conjecture in a current numerical-analysis framework for ACA, shows the failure is robust rather than exceptional, establishes the exact first possible dimension, and demonstrates failure even at an order admitting real Hadamard matrices. It therefore constrains any corrected theory of weighted singular-vector coherence and Hadamard extremality.
